title: Buck Converter (step-down)
summary: Non-isolated step-down converter; in continuous conduction the output voltage equals the input scaled by the duty cycle D.

ports.name: sw
ports.description: Switching node between the high-side switch, the freewheeling diode/synchronous switch, and the inductor.

ports.name: out
ports.description: Regulated step-down output rail across the filter capacitor and load.

ports.name: pwm
ports.description: Gate-drive command for the high-side switch from the controller.

parameters.name: D
parameters.description: Steady-state duty cycle of the high-side switch.

design_equations.name: inductor_current
design_equations.description: Average inductor current equals the load current.

design_equations.name: output_ripple
design_equations.description: Peak-to-peak output voltage ripple for an ideal capacitor.

design_equations.name: critical_inductance
design_equations.description: Minimum inductance to stay in continuous conduction at the given load.

control_notes: The buck control-to-output transfer function is a second-order low-pass with a complex pole pair at the LC resonance and an ESR zero; it has no right-half-plane zero, so voltage-mode control with a Type-II/Type-III compensator is straightforward. Peak/average current-mode control reduces the plant to first order and eases loop design.

reference.source: J. Marcos Alonso, Modelling, Control and Simulation of DC-DC Converters
